title: Read barriers, projection certification, and snapshot publication
purpose: Find reachable temporal-consistency defects in live and query-checkpoint reads: a requested consistency mode may establish the wrong Raft barrier, pinned stores may describe no valid common history, a projection may certify or publish incomplete state, or direct/prepared paths may enforce different temporal preconditions. Follow the companion evidence and ownership contract. Predicate membership, binding, ordering, and pagination at an equivalent fixed horizon and served index version belong to query-semantic-equivalence.
invariants: A default live read executes ReadIndexAndWait, carries the barrier to local execution, and rejects a pinned main snapshot whose durable LastAppliedIndex is below it. A stale read may omit only the quorum barrier; it cannot be labeled default or bypass alignment for a projection it consults.

A request uses one fixed main-store handle and durable horizon H. It waits only for projections consulted, never chases a moving head, and reads each projection certificate from the immutable snapshot supplying the result.

A projection publishes Raft progress H only after folding every relevant source item visible at H. Progress/cursor and all result-affecting writes for that boundary commit atomically; empty Raft entries advance certification when complete, while terminal corruption fails readiness and wakes waiters.

At restart, index dispatch is restored from ledger history and active versions at the durable read-store cursor. A newer main registry cannot apply drops or ledger deletions early: any intermediate checkpoint certificate must include the index writes preceding those lifecycle logs.

A projection snapshot certified beyond H cannot leak newer effects where common-history trimming is required. Transaction/log membership, account event/stamp resolution, enrichment, metadata schema, and served IndexVersionState obey their documented per-target pin rules.

Direct, hardcoded, and prepared executions consulting the same stores enforce the same barrier propagation, fixed main horizon, projection waits, served-version resolution, history lease, trimming, and failure behavior. Fixed-state predicate/result equivalence remains outside this domain.

Index create, rewrite, removal, ledger deletion, and recreation never expose an unready, partially backfilled, stale-version, or deleted keyspace as ready. The served-version switch, rows, reverse-map lifecycle, and progress form one valid transition, and reclamation respects active readers.

A query checkpoint becomes discoverable only after main and read components represent its declared boundary and a ready marker is published last. Interrupted creation leaves no usable partial checkpoint; deletion preserves acquired readers, and a frozen projection behind its main horizon fails instead of waiting or returning partial data.

Audit-index and usage projections expose coherent snapshots under their documented freshness semantics. Historical query-checkpoint responses never mix live usage data into frozen results; asynchronous rebuildability is not mislabeled as strong certification.

Every finding identifies the temporal boundary violated, reachable production path, source and projection positions/versions, and single correction owner. Agreement between readers sharing a projection or helper is not proof of convergence to committed history.
adversarial_questions: For every public read and mode, where is ReadIndexAndWait invoked, how is its index transported, and can a direct, prepared, inspect, audit, stats, or checkpoint path drop or relabel it?
Can a request open the main handle before reserving history, derive H or sequence from another handle, release a lease early, or read the certificate outside the projection snapshot it uses?

Can a builder advance Raft progress or its native cursor before all rows, deletions, registry/version state, audit entries, or counters represented by that position share a successful batch? What is visible after commit, flush, or retry failure?
Do no-log Raft entries, empty ledgers, rollback/reset, terminal corruption, or restart make a waiter hang, accept incomplete empty state, or skip a required position?

Can startup load a registry newer than the durable fold cursor, omit a still-active historical index, and certify missing rows at a checkpoint before replay reaches the later drop or ledger deletion? Does rollback preserve outstanding lifecycle replay obligations?
Can a projection ahead of H leak a post-H transaction/log, metadata event, first-touch row, schema type, or promoted version into enrichment at H?
During create, backfill, retype, drop, delete/recreate, and reclamation, can readiness/version publication precede complete rows or race an active reader into a deleted keyspace?

Can direct and prepared execution differ because one omits OpenReservedQueryHandle, AlignmentOwed, AlignedIndexSnapshot, MainHorizonKeep, version resolution, or release ordering? If state is proven identical, should the evidence instead go to query-semantic-equivalence?

Can checkpoint components represent different boundaries, a markerless directory open, a ready marker survive incomplete creation, deletion invalidate a lease, or a frozen mismatch be treated as transient lag?
Can stats, usage, audit listing, or historical reads stitch peer-store moments, claim stronger freshness than implemented, or combine frozen state with live-only projections?

Is an apparent defect actually restore loss, consensus failure, fixed-state semantics, API representation, or lifecycle cancellation? Which neighboring manifest owns the required correction, and what rejects duplication?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: Build a default/stale write-then-read matrix on leaders and followers. Record barrier R, main H and native sequence, consulted certificates/versions, and response identities; inject lag and leadership transfer at each handoff.

Pause builders between source scan, writes, cursor/progress write, commit, flush, notification, and version promotion. Readers must see a previous complete state, new complete state, or explicit error, never a mixture.

Run direct/hardcoded and prepared calls on an independently seeded non-empty fixture at identical H and served version. Compare temporal-gate traces first; hand remaining fixed-state membership/order differences to query-semantic-equivalence.

Exercise index create/backfill/retype/drop and ledger delete/recreate with concurrent reads and leases, rows around H, no-log entries, restart, and reclamation; verify versions and rejection states against independent history.

Close and reopen both stores with the read index behind main. Start a live read before boot configuration loads, pin it before a later index drop, and hold replay at a checkpoint through audit lag. Require the non-empty pre-drop result at the intermediate certificate; cover restored current/pending/rewrite/tombstone states and ledger-delete rollback separately.

Crash before and after each checkpoint component and ready-marker publication, then enumerate/open it. Acquire/read/delete concurrently; require matching frozen horizons and rejection or rebuild of incomplete directories.

Drive audit-index and usage builders through lag, multi-field reads, flush failure, restart, and primary rollback. Compare every projected key/value with an independent fold and prove historical reads omit live-only usage.

Use existing alignment/horizon, aligned-snapshot, indexbuilder progress/retype/checkpoint, readstore lease/version/progress, usage integration, e2e cross-store/checkpoint, and Antithesis projection tests as leads. Record commands and fault points; green tests or equal totals alone are not proof.
